analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: WAF, SOI up to neutral, AMD, Arista, Block
key_insights: UBS S&T commentary (not UBS Research) says the US election result and Texas/Ohio outcomes dominate the open. Asia has rallied, and the author does not expect the reaction to hold, calling the result 'pretty bad news for AI'.

UBS bottom-up analysts combined expect about 50 GW of compute capacity added in 2027, rising to about 105 GW in 2030. A UBS note by Francois points to a potential shortfall of about 20 GW a year in utility capacity. Meeting semiconductor analyst expectations would require perfect execution of behind-the-meter power. The note is the Global Semiconductors piece 'AI Data Center Power Semis - watts the problem?'.

Siltronic (WAF) Q3 revenue was EUR 355m, 7% above consensus, up 18% y/y and about 11% q/q, driven by wafer demand across 300mm and 200mm. UBS expects low-single-digit % increases to FY26 and FY27 consensus.
Siltronic Q3 EBITDA was EUR 81m vs consensus EUR 72m, 13% above, mainly from higher wafer shipments with limited impact from product mix and price.
Siltronic non-LTA prices edged higher for 300mm and started to stabilise for 200mm, with first positive pricing points in Q3. UBS expects pricing to accelerate into next year.
Siltronic now guides to flat sales y/y vs a prior low-to-mid-single-digit % decline (consensus -2%). It narrowed its EBITDA margin range to 22-24% from 20-24% (consensus 22.7%).

UBS upgrades Soitec to Neutral and raises its PT to EUR 130. Photonics is now expected to reach 50% of revenues by C2028E vs 28% previously, and there is more scope to move smartphone RF SOI capacity to datacenter uses. UBS sees the shares as fairly valued given uncertainty over AI infrastructure spending and smartphone headwinds from macro uncertainty and higher memory prices.
AMD reported solid numbers and guided about in line with UBS's model, better than feared after Intel's guide-down. Server CPU upside more than offsets client downside.

AMD walked up C2027 guidance to a range roughly consistent with UBS's model but well above Street numbers. UBS attributes this to better supply than Intel in wafers and multi-sourced substrates, with both client and server on N2.
AMD 2027 gross margin commentary is consistent with the prior 55-56% messaging. About 60% of incremental data center dollars come from the lower-margin GPU business.

UBS raises AMD EPS to about $19 for C2027E and about $30 for C2028E, and sees about $40 EPS for C2029 as possible even with a significant growth deceleration. It cuts its PT to $700 from $730 because semiconductor multiples have compressed, and keeps Buy.

Arista Q3 revenue was $3.66B, up about 59% y/y, about 10% above UBS's $3.31B estimate (guide $3.3B, Visible Alpha consensus $3.3B). Product revenue was about $3.2B, up about 59% y/y, vs UBS's $2.87B and consensus $2.86B.

Arista gross margin of 64.0% beat the guide of about 63%, UBS's 63.0% and consensus 63.1%, despite a stronger hyperscaler mix. Operating margin of 49.1% was at the high end of the 48-49% guide (UBS 48.5%, consensus 48.9%). Diluted EPS of $1.20 beat UBS's $1.07 by about 12% (guide $1.06-$1.08, consensus $1.08).
Arista guided Q4 revenue to $3.9-$4.0B, about 59% growth at the midpoint, vs UBS's $3.58B and Visible Alpha consensus of $3.60B.

market_movers.rationale: UBS keeps Buy and cuts the PT from $730 to $700 to reflect compressed semiconductor multiples. It raises C2027E EPS to about $19 and C2028E to about $30 on a supply advantage over Intel and server CPU strength.

Soitec is upgraded to Neutral on faster Photonics growth, resilient near-term pricing and room to move smartphone RF SOI capacity to datacenter. Shares are seen as fairly valued given AI spending and smartphone risks.
Q3 revenue, gross margin, operating margin and EPS all beat UBS estimates and consensus. Q4 revenue guidance of $3.9-$4.0B is above UBS's $3.58B and consensus of $3.60B.

sector_views.rationale: Positive supplier and AI hardware earnings (AMD, Arista, Siltronic) sit against a power-capacity constraint on AI data center buildout and an election-driven risk to AI sentiment.

earnings_insights: Siltronic Q3 reported revenue EUR 355m, 7% above consensus, up 18% y/y. Reported EBITDA EUR 81m vs consensus EUR 72m (13% above).
Siltronic FY guide, issued with Q3 results: sales flat y/y vs a prior low-to-mid-single-digit % decline (consensus -2%). EBITDA margin range 22-24% vs 20-24% previously (consensus 22.7%).

AMD reported solid results and guided about in line with UBS's model. C2027 guidance was walked up to a range roughly consistent with UBS and well above Street. UBS C2027E EPS is about $19 and C2028E about $30 (UBS estimates).
Arista Q3 reported revenue $3.66B vs UBS est $3.31B and Visible Alpha consensus $3.3B. Reported diluted EPS $1.20 vs UBS est $1.07 and consensus $1.08.
Arista Q3 reported gross margin 64.0% vs guide of about 63% and consensus 63.1%. Reported operating margin 49.1% vs consensus 48.9%.
Arista Q4:26 guidance of revenue $3.9-$4.0B (59% growth at midpoint) vs UBS est $3.58B and Visible Alpha consensus $3.60B.
risk_factors: US election outcome could reverse the Asia rally and hurt AI-linked names, in the author's view.
A potential 20 GW per year shortfall in utility capacity for AI data centers, which would require perfect behind-the-meter execution to meet semiconductor analyst expectations.
Soitec: uncertainty over AI infrastructure spending, and smartphone headwinds from macro uncertainty and higher memory prices.
AMD: about 60% of incremental data center dollars come from the lower-margin GPU business, a gross margin headwind. Semiconductor multiples have compressed.
geopolitical: US election result and Texas/Ohio outcomes are the focus at the open, with Asia having rallied.
